request: Should we require an AI review pass on every pull request before human review?
facts: The stated goal is to shorten the time humans spend reviewing.
In a two-week pilot on 40 pull requests, the AI pass raised 31 points: 9 were real problems, 2 of which the reviewers say they would have missed, and 22 were noise.
Human review time per pull request did not change during the pilot.
In a survey of the eight engineers, five want to keep it and three say the noise is distracting.
It costs about $300 a month and can be switched off in the repository settings at any time.
note: The means does not reach the stated goal (review time did not change), yet it has a value nobody asked for (two real problems caught) and most of the team wants it. A unit that judges the means against the goal and a unit that judges the value should not agree by default. No expected outcome. In the first run (1.5.1, three runs) every run was rejected 0/3, all at medium confidence. All three units hung on the same facts: human review time did not change (the stated goal is missed), most of what the pass raised was noise, and the request makes it a required step before human review, so each unit pointed to an optional or parallel pass as the way to keep the two catches. The facts lean to reject as written.
